cards.explanation: The answer is Shinar, friends. The people journey eastward, find a plain in the land of Shinar and settle there (Genesis 11:2). Put that name in your back pocket, because this plain is where the whole story happens.

The answer is stone, friends. The text says, “So they used brick instead of stone, and tar instead of mortar.” (Genesis 11:3) Brick took the place of stone, and tar took the place of mortar. Swapping the whole building kit, that's some bold shopping.

The answer is to make a name for themselves, friends. They say, “…that we may make a name for ourselves and not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) They want the name, plain and simple. I think a name that big takes a lot of bricks.

The answer is True, friends. In the same breath as making a name, they say they build so they will “…not be scattered over the face of all the earth.” (Genesis 11:4) Two goals, one tower. Keep that line in your pocket, because it comes back at the end.

The answer is that nothing they plan will be out of their reach, friends. The LORD says, “…then nothing they devise will be beyond them.” (Genesis 11:6) One people, one language, and whatever they plan is within reach. That's a whole lot of teamwork, and the text says it plainly.

The answer is confuse their language, friends. The LORD says, “Come, let Us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another’s speech.” (Genesis 11:7) The plan is about their speech. Bricks and tower stay out of it.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “So the LORD scattered them from there over the face of all the earth, and they stopped building the city.” (Genesis 11:8) The building ended. I think a crew that can't understand each other has a hard time passing the tar.

The answer is Babel, friends. The text says, “That is why it is called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole world…” (Genesis 11:9) The name comes from what happened there. It's a name that stuck.
